title: Smoked Salmon Omelette
subtitle: A delicate omelette filled with cold-smoked salmon and crème fraîche
excerpt: Cold-smoked salmon and a spoonful of crème fraîche folded into a barely-set French omelette, a ten-minute breakfast that eats like a special occasion.
sourceNotes: Smoked salmon as an omelette filling is a modern British-French combination, common in upmarket cafés and hotel breakfasts. The crème fraîche addition is a contemporary refinement that balances the salt of the salmon.

glossaryTerms.definition: Rolling one side of the omelette over the filling using a spatula, then tipping the pan to roll the whole omelette onto the plate with the seam underneath, enclosing the filling inside a neat, closed egg parcel.

content.text: Smoked salmon and crème fraîche folded into a barely-set omelette is a light, elegant breakfast that takes under five minutes once the technique is familiar. The salmon goes in cold, it warms from the residual heat of the egg without cooking, staying silky and retaining its texture. The crème fraîche cuts through the salt of the salmon and adds a gentle creaminess to the centre. Season carefully: smoked salmon is already salty, so taste before adding any extra salt.

Tear the {{smoked-salmon}} smoked salmon into rough pieces, not too small, so they retain presence inside the omelette. Have the {{creme-fraiche}} crème fraîche and most of the {{chives}} chives ready beside the pan. Everything should be assembled before you start beating the eggs, because the omelette stage takes less than a minute and there is no time to prepare anything mid-cook.

Beat the {{eggs}} eggs well and season with {{black-pepper}} black pepper only. The salmon will provide all the salt needed. Heat the 20 cm frying pan over medium-high heat for a full minute, add {{unsalted-butter}} butter, and let it foam and begin to subside. Pour in the egg. Shake the pan and draw the spatula across the base in short strokes for twenty to twenty-five seconds, until the egg is almost set with just a thin wet layer on top.
Scatter the salmon pieces across the centre of the omelette in a strip. Spoon the crème fraîche in small dots alongside the salmon, it will melt slightly and distribute as the omelette is

. Add most of the chives. Tilt the pan, fold the near third of the omelette over the centre, and roll it onto a warm plate seam-side down. Scatter the remaining chives over the top. Taste before reaching for salt.

A smoked salmon omelette suits a weekend rather than a hurried weekday, not because it is particularly difficult, but because it deserves to be eaten slowly. It goes well with a small green salad if you want to stretch it into a light brunch, or with good brown toast and something cold and fizzy if you are feeling indulgent. It is also a very good way to use the last 60 g of smoked salmon from a packet that is already open.

Omelette is too salty: smoked salmon varies considerably in salt content. If the salmon is particularly salty, use no additional seasoning at all and let the crème fraîche do the work of balancing it.

Salmon has turned opaque and cooked: the egg was too hot when the salmon went in, or the omelette sat in the pan too long before rolling. Work quickly, the filling goes in the moment you stop shaking the pan, and the roll follows immediately.
Crème fraîche has split and turned watery: it heated too long inside the omelette. Add it cold at the last moment and roll immediately, it only needs a few seconds of residual warmth to soften.
